question: In Figure 6L-3, which arrow-board mode is required in addition to at least one directional merge mode and at least one caution mode?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The Flashing Double Arrow mode is the mode that must be provided in addition to the others. Figure 6L-3 and Section 6L.06 require an arrow board to have three mode selections: at least one directional mode (Flashing Arrow, Sequential Arrow, or Sequential Chevron), the flashing Double Arrow mode, and at least one caution mode (flashing Caution or Alternating Diamond). Standards (mandatory): - "An arrow board shall have the following three mode selections: A. A Flashing Arrow, Sequential Arrow, or Sequential Chevron mode; B. A flashing Double Arrow mode; and C. A flashing Caution or Alternating Diamond mode." - "Arrow boards shall meet the minimum size, legibility distance, number of elements, and other specifications shown in Figure 6L-3." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 6L-3 lists item 2 as "The following mode shall be provided: Flashing Double Arrow," illustrated as a "Merge Right or Left" display, whereas items 1 and 3 each require only "at least one" of the listed directional or caution modes. Citations: - Section 6L.06 Standard §16 (p.833) - Section 6L.06 Standard §5 (p.833) - Figure 6L-3 (p.834)
